stakeholder = anyone with an interest in an organisation, including staff, customers and neighbours
shareholder = a person or body that owns shares in a company
return on investment = the profit from money put into a venture, relative to what was spent
side hustle = paid work done besides a main job
portfolio career = earning a living from several part-time roles or clients at once
coworking space = a shared office rented by freelancers and small firms
staggered hours = a system in which staff start and finish at different times to spread demand
long-term unemployment = being out of work and looking for a job for a year or more
jobseeker = a person who is looking for paid work
underemployment = having a job that uses too few hours or too little of your skill
job security = how safe your post is from sudden loss
precarious work = insecure employment with unstable hours, pay or rights
career ladder = the sequence of more senior posts in a field
dead-end job = a post with no real chance of progress or skill growth
clock off = to record the time you finish work, often on a machine
core hours = the part of the day when flexitime staff must be at work
employment tribunal = a specialist court that hears disputes about work rights
upskilling = training existing staff in additional skills for current or future tasks
reskilling = training people for a different kind of work after their old role disappears
on-the-job training = learning a role by doing it under supervision, rather than in a classroom
